prompts.prompt:
[FORMAT]
Vertical 2:3 Pinterest pin composition.

[SUBJECT]
Extreme close-up of a hand holding a fine-tip pen, writing across the open page of a worn personal journal. The handwriting is rendered as loose, gestural abstract ink strokes and flowing cursive-like scribble marks — no legible words, no readable sentences, no real letters, purely expressive line work suggesting the rhythm of writing. A single small four-leaf clover sticker is placed casually in the upper-right margin of the page, slightly crooked, with a faint adhesive shadow beneath it.

[COMPOSITION]
Vertical 2:3 framing. The hand and pen occupy the lower two-thirds of the frame, anchored left of center using rule of thirds. Abstract ink strokes sweep diagonally across the page, guiding the eye from upper-left to lower-right. The clover sticker sits in the upper-right third, acting as a quiet visual counterweight. Generous warm paper texture fills the background — no props compete. Top of frame opens with aged paper grain to stop the scroll. Hand-crafted, intimate, not staged.

[AESTHETIC]
Pinterest-native: warm, hand-crafted, lived-in. Quiet-luxury meets cottagecore journaling ritual. Soft morning light filtering across paper. The feeling of a private, unhurried moment — a personal resolution being committed to the page.

[LIGHTING]
Golden hour motivated practical light entering from 45° camera-left. Large softbox diffusion quality mimicking warm window light. Color temperature 3800K mixed warm-tungsten. Gentle highlight rolloff across the paper surface, catching the slight sheen of fresh ink and the texture of the page grain. Soft falloff with gradient transition into the right edge of frame. No harsh shadows — contact shadow only at the pen nib and fingertips where they press the page.

[SURFACE & TEXTURE]
Aged paper with visible laid-line texture and slight cream-yellow warmth — not white, not sterile. Subtle paper grain catches the raking light. The journal cover edge visible at the bottom frame in worn leather. The clover sticker has a matte vinyl finish with micro-emboss detail on the leaf veins.

[COLOR PALETTE]
Muted Pinterest palette: warm parchment, soft ochre, dusty sage (from the clover sticker), and deep sepia-brown ink strokes. Skin tones warm and natural, not retouched. No neon, no oversaturation. The entire palette sits within a golden-amber register.

[CAMERA]
100mm macro lens. f/2.8. Shallow depth of field — pen nib and ink strokes tack-sharp, hand softly in focus, journal edges and background dissolving into warm bokeh. 85mm portrait alternative acceptable for slightly wider context.

[STYLE REFERENCE]
In the style of Beth Kirby, Brittany Ambridge, and Pia Ulin. Editorial Pinterest journaling aesthetic — intimate, save-worthy, magazine-quality.

[QUALITY MARKERS]
Save-worthy, scroll-stopping, magazine-quality, hyper-detailed paper texture, photorealistic ink and skin rendering, warm film-adjacent color grading.

[AVOID]
no AI artifacts, no warped or smeared text, no fake words baked into the image,
no plastic look, no waxy surface, no cartoonish rendering,
no extra fingers, no extra limbs, no melted geometry, no doubled subjects,
no oversaturated HDR, no HDR halos, no oversharpened look,
no flat fluorescent lighting, no harsh on-camera flash,
no generic stock photography poses, no cliché compositions,
no random unrelated brand logos, no watermarks, no signatures,
no AI sheen on hair or skin, no doll-like rendering, no airbrush look,
no flat solid color bands, no empty rectangular areas, no dull gradient zones,
no AI uncanny faces, no warped facial geometry, no plastic skin,
no readable letters, no legible words, no actual sentences, no recognizable alphabet characters in the ink strokes,
no sterile studio feel, no oversaturated colors, no neon,
no Instagram-grid square framing, no horizontal-leaning compositions,
no stale stock photography aesthetic, no synthetic stock-photo look,
no over-staged feeling, no unrealistically clean environments.

resolution: 2k
